Case Study Content Brief: AOM as Case Study #1

Date: 2026-03-12 Authors: Alex (Deal Architect) + Steve (AI Advisory Lead) Page: aheadofmarket.com/case-study Purpose: Turn AOM's internal AI system into the #1 sales proof asset for the AI advisory product.

Why This Exists

Every prospect Jacob emails, every LinkedIn visitor, every CPA who runs the ROI calculator has the same question: "Has anyone actually done this?"

The answer is AOM itself. But the proof is buried in repo commits and context files. This page puts it on a stage.

The case study sits between the ROI calculator ("here's what the numbers could look like for you") and the audit booking ("let's make it real"). Without it, AOM is selling a concept. With it, AOM is showing a running system.

Target Reader

Primary: CPA or contractor with 3-15 employees. Skeptical about AI. Has heard the hype. Doesn't know where to start. Currently doing everything manually or with a patchwork of SaaS tools.

What they're thinking when they land on this page:

  • "This sounds too good to be true."
  • "Show me proof."
  • "What does this actually look like?"
  • "How much did it cost? How long did it take?"

What they should think when they leave:

  • "They actually built this. It's real."
  • "If they did it for themselves, they can do it for me."
  • "Let me see what the numbers look like for my business."

The Narrative Arc

Act 1: The Problem (Relatability)

AOM is a two-person creative production company in Phoenix. Video, web, brand, social. Patrik Matheson runs it. Every client email, every invoice follow-up, every social post, every proposal, every project status check... all manual. All Patrik.

The bottleneck wasn't talent or hustle. It was time. One person physically cannot:

  • Produce creative work
  • Run the back office
  • Do outreach
  • Manage client relationships
  • Maintain quality control

Something always slips. Leads die in the inbox. Client relationships cool because nobody follows up. Brand consistency is a coin flip. Quality control only happens when Patrik personally reviews everything.

The reader should see themselves here. Every small business owner does everything. This is their life.

Act 2: The Decision (The Turn)

Instead of hiring (6 figures in salary, months of ramp-up, training, management overhead), Patrik built a system. Using Claude Code as the foundation, he created specialized AI agents, each owning one part of the business.

Not a chatbot. Not a plugin. Not a SaaS dashboard with limited automation. A full operations layer that works 24/7.

The thesis: if a solo creative agency can build an AI system that handles its own outreach, QA, client tracking, brand enforcement, and operational oversight, then that same system can be packaged and sold to any small business.

AOM became the builder AND the proof of concept.

Pull quote: "Isn't it smart for me as a small business owner to help build tailored solutions for people since I've been able to do it for myself?"

Act 3: The System (What Was Built)

12 specialized AI agents, each with a defined role, working in a pipeline:

The Pipeline: Elon (System) > Mom (Operations) > Alex (Strategy) > Steffen (Brand) > Bobby (Build) > Elmo (QA) > Patrik (Approve)

Every deliverable flows through this chain automatically. Patrik only touches the final approval.

The Agents:

Agent Role What It Replaced
Jacob Outreach Engine Manual copy-paste emails with no tracking
Mom Chief of Staff Patrik mentally juggling every open task
Paige Client Health Client relationships tracked in Patrik's head
Elmo Quality Gate Bugs only caught when Patrik personally reviewed everything
Bobby Web Builder Weeks of development time per page
Steffen Brand Director Inconsistent visual identity across deliverables
Cleo Content Producer Manual video editing and content workflows
Tony Social Media Manual posting, no scheduling, no multi-platform
Elon System Admin No infrastructure monitoring, no credential rotation
Alex Deal Architect Offer strategy done ad-hoc, never documented
Steve AI Advisory Lead No product packaging, no ROI modeling
Relay 24/7 Bridge Messages sitting unread until morning

Supporting infrastructure:

  • 29+ skills (reusable workflows)
  • Telegram relay with <2s response time
  • Watchdog for 24/7 uptime
  • RAG layer for semantic knowledge search
  • Decision log for institutional memory
  • Session log for continuity across conversations

Act 4: The Results (Hard Numbers)

These are real, verifiable numbers from the running system:

Metric Number Context
Specialized AI agents 12+ Running 24/7
Commits shipped 280+ In the first 2 weeks
Time to build a new page ~2 hours From spec to live on site
Outreach emails sent 51+ In a single batch. 56+ in pipeline. Personalized, tracked.
Pages/tools shipped 8+ Dashboard, ROI calculator, booking flow, ideas tracker, 8 brief pages, audit tool
Additional headcount cost $0 Zero new hires
Relay response time <2 seconds Best case, hook-based injection
Operational uptime 24/7 Relay + watchdog + launchd agents
Skills built 29+ Reusable agent workflows
Cost comparison $200-280k/year traditional vs. fraction of one hire Outreach coordinator + QA + PM + brand manager combined

The Cost Comparison (detailed):

Role Traditional Salary AOM's System
Outreach coordinator $45-65k/year Jacob agent, $0
QA tester $50-70k/year Elmo: Playwright screenshots + accessibility
Project manager $55-75k/year Mom agent, always on
Brand manager $50-70k/year Steffen agent + design standards
After-hours coverage Overtime or missed messages 24/7 relay with watchdog
Total $200-280k/year System cost: fraction of one hire

Hours saved estimate:

Based on what the agents handle vs. what Patrik was doing manually:

  • Outreach: ~10 hrs/week (researching, writing, sending, tracking 50+ emails)
  • QA: ~5 hrs/week (manually checking every page at every breakpoint)
  • Client tracking: ~3 hrs/week (checking in, logging status, following up)
  • Brand enforcement: ~3 hrs/week (reviewing every deliverable for consistency)
  • Operations routing: ~5 hrs/week (deciding what to do next, assigning work)
  • System maintenance: ~2 hrs/week (monitoring, credential rotation, health checks)
  • Total: ~28 hrs/week recovered (equivalent to a full-time employee's productive hours)

Act 5: A Day in the Life (Proof It's Real)

A concrete timeline showing what 24 hours looks like with the system running:

Time What Happens
7:00 AM Patrik sends a Telegram message: "Check Ambition site, footer looks off on mobile."
7:01 AM Relay picks it up. Message injected via hook. No polling, no delay.
7:02 AM Bobby launches. Reads the request, pulls the repo, identifies the issue.
7:08 AM Fix committed. Mom auto-launches.
7:09 AM Elmo QA runs. Screenshots the page at 5 breakpoints. Checks for regressions.
7:12 AM Patrik gets confirmation: "Footer fixed. Elmo QA passed. Live on site."
While Patrik's on a shoot... Jacob sends 15 outreach emails. Paige scans client health. Steffen catches a font-weight deviation.
11:00 PM Patrik's asleep. Message comes in. Watchdog sends a "compressing" notice. Defers for morning.

12 minutes from request to live fix, with QA. While Patrik was probably still pouring coffee.

Act 6: The Bridge (What This Means for You)

Everything on the page is real. It's running as the reader reads it. The agents that built the website are the same agents that sent the email or LinkedIn post that brought them there.

The question isn't whether AI can run a small business's back office. AOM proved it can. The question is what it would look like for THEIR business.

Three paths forward:

  1. See Your Numbers - ROI calculator. 6 inputs, 30 seconds.
  2. Get the Full Picture - $2,500 AI Operations Audit. Custom roadmap.
  3. Talk to Us - 15-minute call, no cost.

Metrics Source Map

For Patrik's approval (what's being shared publicly):

  • 12+ agents (number and general descriptions, not architecture)
  • 280+ commits metric
  • "Pages built in ~2 hours" claim
  • 51+ outreach emails sent
  • $0 additional headcount framing
  • 24/7 operations claim

Nothing exposes proprietary architecture, prompt engineering, or technical implementation. All outcomes and structure.

  2. Agent cards grid - 12 cards showing each agent's name, role, what it does
  3. Metrics callout cards - Large numbers with labels and context
  4. Cost comparison table - Traditional vs. AOM system, responsive
  5. Timeline visualization - Vertical timeline with timestamps and event cards
  6. Before/after pain points grid - What the problem looked like vs. the solution

  • Micro-labels: JetBrains Mono 700, 9-11px, uppercase, tracking-[0.3em]
  • Orange accent: #E85D26

Funnel Position

The case study is the trust layer between "who are these people?" and "take my money."
